studies.title: Benchmark scores by task
studies.locator: Results: domain-dependent performance; July 2026 version of record
studies.credit: Kim et al. / Nature Machine Intelligence / 2026
studies.note: Mean scores across tested models. The best multi-agent architecture is selected separately for each benchmark. Matched system token ceilings; actual spending can differ. No pooled score or significance claim.
studies.alt: Single-agent and best multi-agent mean scores across six benchmarks. Multi-agent scores are higher on Finance Agent, WorkBench, BrowseComp-Plus, and Terminal-Bench; single-agent scores are higher on PlanCraft and SWE-bench Verified.

studies.title: Accuracy across requested token budgets
studies.note: Table 1 averages over four models × two datasets (FRAMES and MuSiQue). Requested token ceilings, not identical actual consumption. The token axis is logarithmic. Three of the seven evaluated methods are shown.
studies.alt: Debate leads at 100 requested thinking tokens. The single-agent average leads the three displayed methods at every budget from 500 to 10,000 tokens. At 1,000 tokens: 41.8% single agent, 37.9% sequential agents, 38.8% debate.

studies.title: Accuracy at comparable modeled compute
studies.locator: Section 4.1 and Section 8; ACL SRW, July 2026
studies.note: Llama 3.1 70B; 1,000 MMLU-Pro questions. Best reported configurations within the tested compute range. Whiskers are approximate 95% binomial intervals, calculated using the paper's formula. These are not intervals on the differences.
studies.alt: Accuracy is 68.7% for self-consistency, 70.0% for debate, and 71.4% for mixture of agents. Approximate individual 95% intervals overlap. Mixture of agents gains 2.7 percentage points over self-consistency.
studies.derivation: Individual 95% interval: 100 × [p ± 1.96 × sqrt(p × (1 − p) / 1000)], p = reported accuracy / 100. Rounded source estimates; no paired significance inference.

studies.title: The four cost-matched SwarmBench tasks
studies.locator: Table 7, Appendix D.1; metrics in Appendix C.1; v1, 31 August 2026
studies.note: Haiku 4.5 single agent and orchestrator; heterogeneous workers; 50 examples per task. Single-agent spending is capped at each task's mean swarm cost. Different metrics and axis ranges; no combined accuracy. No comparison intervals are supplied.
studies.alt: At matched cost ceilings, swarm scores exceed single-agent scores for multi-text understanding, long-text generation, and wide search. Single-agent root-cause analysis scores are higher. Only four of the eight benchmark tasks have this comparison.

studies.title: Research performance and typical token use
studies.locator: Internal research evaluation and token-use observations; 13 June 2025
studies.note: Two separate observations, not a paired efficiency experiment. Performance uses an Opus 4 lead with Sonnet 4 workers against one Opus 4 agent. Absolute evaluation scores are undisclosed. Token multiples describe typical use relative to chat.
studies.alt: Internal research performance: single-agent index 100, multi-agent index 190.2, derived from a 90.2% relative gain. Separate typical token-use observation: chat about 1×, single agent about 4×, multi-agent about 15×. Neither index is an accuracy percentage.
studies.derivation: Performance index: 100 × (1 + 90.2 / 100) = 190.2. This is a normalized illustration of the reported relative improvement, not a reported absolute score. Do not combine with the separate typical token-use observation to calculate evaluation efficiency.

studies.title: Workflow execution: pass rate and latency
studies.note: Qwen3 8B on HumanEval; vLLM, 16k context, three-run means. Table 4 reports no uncertainty intervals. Compare execution methods within each workflow. Token budgets are not matched; latency and pass rate have separate axes.
studies.alt: AFlow: single-conversation pass rate 90.5% versus stateless calls 86.8%; latency 53.53 versus 54.98 seconds. OneFlow: 87.4% versus 87.0%; latency 4.83 versus 4.31 seconds. Single-conversation execution is slightly slower for OneFlow.

studies.title: Fourteen failure modes, grouped by category
studies.locator: Appendix A.1–A.3, printed pages 24–25; final NeurIPS 2025 paper
studies.note: Each square represents one distinct taxonomy label. Counts describe the taxonomy's structure, not failure frequency, severity, or production reliability. There is no single-agent control group.
studies.alt: The MAST taxonomy has five system-design modes, six inter-agent misalignment modes, and three task-verification modes. These are counts of identified categories, not counts of observed failures.
